statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) in every hour of the CME weekend halt; Stress 25 (moderate); Confidence 63 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, which is the exact end of this forecast window, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any hour covered here and Tail remains far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs 25 to 39 inside the moderate band as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence eases from 63 to a 60 floor because the reference tape is ageing rather than because the evidence has become conflicting. No danger window is published, since the first hour in which observable Nasdaq-100 structure can exist begins as this window closes.
headline: Weekend halt, hour 26: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%), NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, the 10-year near 4.72% and a coin-flip September Fed meeting after Warsh; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, which coincides with the end of this forecast window, so every hour assessed here is a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. The pre-halt evidence set was re-verified against primary sources this run: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range against a 29,695.75 previous close; VIX finished at 14.43 within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The dominant driver remains Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, read as hawkish: current reporting describes the September meeting as close to a coin flip, with hike odds repriced into a roughly 54 to 59 percent range from about 34 to 35 percent beforehand, the policy-sensitive 2-year yield touching about 4.32 percent intraday and the 10-year quoted near 4.72 percent. The Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column, at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year, because the release is not posted at weekends. Friday's decline was narrow rather than broad: across the tracked semiconductor set the mean change was minus 2.49 percent, led by Arm down 6.33 percent and Nvidia down 4.57 percent, while five of eight tracked megacaps advanced, with Amazon up 3.97 percent, Alphabet up 1.74 percent and Microsoft up 1.68 percent, leaving megacap dispersion near 2.5 percentage points. Cross-asset weekend context is internally consistent with the hawkish repricing: the dollar index firmed about 0.5 percent and gold fell roughly 3.2 percent to near 4,456 dollars. Energy was orderly into the weekend, with WTI at 83.44 dollars and Brent at 88.29 dollars, and this run's geopolitical check identified no fresh verified supply discontinuity. Weekend information flow has been commentary rather than event risk: verified items include Friday's reporting on the repricing of rate-hike expectations and Saturday's published commentary from Adam Posen on the Fed's forecast communication, a Saturday global economy briefing summarising the same repricing, and a Saturday feature on new futures tied to Nvidia GPU rental prices. None of that can reach a price until the venue reopens. Tail is therefore held at 5 in all 24 slots, which maps to EA_ON and green throughout and publishes no danger window, because a closed market cannot produce the shallow pullbacks, failed retracements, repeated extension or session-extreme holding that Tail measures. Stress rises from 25 to 39 inside the moderate band as the stock of unpriced weekend information grows into the reopen and the 1 to 4 September data stack. Confidence eases from 63 to a 60 floor, remaining in the solid band because the evidence is complete and primary-source verified and is ageing rather than becoming conflicted.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from the post-close futures hour on Friday through hour 25 of the weekend halt. The mode was normal in every slot and the mapped policy state never left EA_ON. Tail decayed from 7 to 5 within the first three hours and then held the 5 floor for the remaining twenty-one, because no venue was open to produce the price-path evidence Tail is defined against. Stress fell to a 22 trough in the early hours of Saturday and then held a 25 plateau for the last seventeen hours, while Confidence declined steadily from 85 to 64 as the Friday reference tape aged without any new observable structure. No hour in the window carried a danger window and no hour was unavailable.
outlookSummary: Every hour of the forecast window falls inside the CME weekend halt, which ends exactly as the window closes at Sunday 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any slot; Tail is held at 5 throughout, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON with no danger window, and the dominant mode is normal in every slot because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress ramps from 25 to 39 in the moderate band, rising with the stock of unpriced weekend information ahead of the reopen and of the 1 to 4 September data stack of ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS, ADP, Broadcom results, ISM Services and the August payrolls report, with the 15 to 16 September FOMC meeting priced close to a coin flip behind it. Confidence eases from 63 to a 60 floor, staying in the solid band because the evidence set is complete and primary-source verified even as the reference tape ages past forty-eight hours by the final slot. The first hour in which observable Nasdaq-100 structure can exist begins as this window ends, so any gap or continuation at the reopen is a checkpoint for a later assessment rather than a published risk here.
